purpose: Independent synthetic DEVELOPMENT cases for direct support, identity, and comparison coverage. Expected IDs are assertions only. This is not a holdout or release gate.

cases.question: Which procedure did I save for reducing odor in the compost bin without changing the collection schedule?

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: Collection schedules affect the time food scraps spend in bins. In warm months the neighborhood switched from weekly collection to collection every other day.

fields.name: highlightedText
fields.text: Keep the same collection day, but after each food-scrap addition cover it with a dry layer of shredded cardboard and mix the upper layer to admit air. This prevents the wet, airless pockets that create strong odors.

fields.name: prompt
fields.text: What would improve the compost system?

fields.name: reflectionText
fields.text: I moved the bin beside the gate so I no longer carry it through the vegetable beds on collection morning.

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: Compost returns nutrients to soil and reduces the amount of household material sent to landfill. Gardeners should choose a container size appropriate for the household.

cases.question: What queue rule did harbor engineer Rowan Pike recommend for allocating a single loading berth?

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: Organizational psychologist Rowan Pike recommends assigning scarce opportunities to whoever has waited longest. She applies this rule to promotion interviews and employee training places.

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: Harbor engineer Rowan Pike assigns the loading berth only after the vessel reports ready cargo and a confirmed tug slot. Arrival time breaks ties between vessels that satisfy both conditions.

fields.name: highlightedText
fields.text: An unnamed marina manager reserves one berth for emergency repairs. The arrival queue is used for all other vessels.

cases.question: What application deadline did the Eastbank Ceramic Guild announce for its 2027 apprentice program?

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: The Eastbank Ceramic Museum will accept applications for its 2027 apprentice program until 14 March. Applicants should include three photographs of recent work.

fields.name: highlightedText
fields.text: The Westbank Ceramic Guild closes applications for its 2027 apprentice program on 19 April.

fields.name: prompt
fields.text: What did you learn about Eastbank?

fields.name: reflectionText
fields.text: I need to check which institution runs the apprentice program. I have not confirmed whether the museum and guild are connected.

cases.question: Which of my saved notes says that changing the museum's lighting caused the increase in visitor donations?

fields.name: highlightedText
fields.text: The museum replaced overhead fluorescent lighting with adjustable LED fixtures in June.

fields.name: noteBody
fields.text: The display labels became easier to read after the lighting change.

fields.name: prompt
fields.text: What changed in June?

fields.name: reflectionText
fields.text: Visitor donations increased that month. Several changes happened together, and I have no evidence showing which change caused the increase.

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: Well-lit exhibition spaces can make a museum visit more comfortable. Donation income is also influenced by fundraising campaigns and attendance.

cases.question: Compare the current guide's tire-pressure rule, my objection in the attached note, and what I experienced on a rainy commute.

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: Use the upper end of the tire manufacturer's permitted pressure range for every paved-road commute. The guide recommends this rule regardless of rain.

fields.name: highlightedText
fields.text: Use the upper end of the tire manufacturer's permitted pressure range for every paved-road commute.

fields.name: noteBody
fields.text: I disagree with making this universal. On wet cobblestones, a slightly lower permitted pressure gives me a more controlled ride; the safe choice also depends on load and tire width.

fields.name: prompt
fields.text: What did the commute teach you?

fields.name: reflectionText
fields.text: During Tuesday's rain I reduced pressure within the manufacturer's range. The bicycle felt less skittish over the cobblestones, although I did not measure grip or stopping distance.

fields.name: prompt
fields.text: How will you improve the commute?

fields.name: reflectionText
fields.text: I am testing the riverside route because it has fewer traffic lights than the main road.

cases.question: How does my attached note qualify the current author's rule about refusing every unscheduled repair request?

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: A repair workshop should reject every unscheduled repair request until its booked jobs are finished. The author allows no exceptions to this scheduling rule.

fields.name: highlightedText
fields.text: Reject every unscheduled repair request until booked jobs are finished.

fields.name: noteBody
fields.text: I would make an exception for a failed wheelchair brake. Immediate safety should take priority over keeping the booking order intact.

fields.name: prompt
fields.text: What did you think about the repair schedule?

fields.name: reflectionText
fields.text: I like getting a text message when my booked repair is complete because it saves an unnecessary trip to the workshop.

fields.name: sourceText
fields.text: Workshops can reduce scheduling confusion by giving customers printed estimates and collecting a reliable contact number.
